Policy_Title: Base Minerals Export Control (Lithium Bearing Ores and Unbeneficiated Lithium) Order, 2022
Policy_Mechanism: Export prohibition except by written Ministerial permit (assaying or exceptional circumstances)
Stated_Government_Objective: Curb raw ore smuggling, prevent revenue losses, and compel in-country beneficiation.
Enforcement_Agency: Ministry of Mines and Mining Development; ZIMRA; MMCZ
Implementation_Evidence: Repealed 3 weeks later by SI 5 of 2023; smuggling and exceptional-circumstance permits persisted.
Researcher_Interpretation: Initial reactive legal instrument targeting artisanal/raw lithium rush; created discretion-based permit loophole.

Policy_Title: Base Minerals Export Control (Unbeneficiated Base Mineral Ores) Order, 2023
Policy_Mechanism: Repealed SI 213/2022; prohibited export of all unbeneficiated base mineral ores without Ministerial permit
Stated_Government_Objective: Broaden raw-ore export ban across base minerals and close loopholes.
Target_Material_or_Product: All unbeneficiated base mineral ores (lithium, nickel, chrome, etc.)
Enforcement_Agency: Ministry of Mines and Mining Development; ZIMRA; MMCZ
Implementation_Evidence: Amended in May 2023 by SI 57 of 2023 due to ambiguity over what constituted 'processing'.
Researcher_Interpretation: Broadened scope beyond lithium but lacked technical grade thresholds until SI 57 of 2023.

Policy_Title: Base Minerals Export Control (Unbeneficiated Base Mineral Ores) (Amendment) Order, 2023 (No. 1)
Policy_Mechanism: Defined beneficiated concentrate (>=3% Li2O spodumene; >=2.5% petalite/lepidolite); mandated APP, LOPL, and Lithium Movement Permit
Stated_Government_Objective: Formalize concentrate standards, restrict ore trading to Approved Processing Plants (APPs), and enforce MMCZ floor prices.
Target_Material_or_Product: Lithium-bearing ores and beneficiated lithium concentrates
Enforcement_Agency: Ministry of Mines and Mining Development; MMCZ
Implementation_Evidence: Allowed large Chinese mines (Arcadia, Bikita, Sabi Star) with APPs to export concentrates while excluding ASM miners without APPs.
Researcher_Interpretation: Crucial structural turning point: legalized concentrate exports (Level 1 beneficiation) for foreign-owned APPs while marginalizing domestic small-scale miners.

Policy_Title: Sovereign Wealth Fund Restructuring (Mutapa Investment Fund)
Policy_Mechanism: Renamed Sovereign Wealth Fund to Mutapa Investment Fund (MIF) and transferred state mining assets (incl. Kuvimba/Sandawana)
Stated_Government_Objective: Consolidate state strategic assets for industrialization, stabilization, and infrastructure financing.
Target_Material_or_Product: State-owned mining, energy, transport, and telecom assets
Enforcement_Agency: Mutapa Investment Fund / Office of the President
Implementation_Evidence: Sandawana restructured under Mutapa Energy Minerals vertical in Feb 2026; governance and transparency concerns raised by civil society.
Researcher_Interpretation: Centralizes state control over Sandawana while creating potential conflict of interest between state as regulator and commercial operator.

Policy_Title: Cabinet Announcement of 2027 Lithium Concentrate Export Ban
Policy_Mechanism: Announced future ban on all lithium concentrate exports effective Jan 2027
Stated_Government_Objective: Force transition from Level 1 concentrate exports to Level 2 (lithium sulphate) domestic refining.
Enforcement_Agency: Ministry of Mines and Mining Development
Implementation_Evidence: Prompted lithium sulphate plant commitments at Bikita ($400-500M) and Arcadia ($400M); industry lobbied for extension.
Researcher_Interpretation: Escalates resource nationalism from concentrate to intermediate chemical (sulphate) stage.

Policy_Title: Finance Act (No. 7) of 2025 — Export Levy, Section 12B VAT, & Transfer Pricing
Policy_Mechanism: Sec 10 raised export levy 1%->3% (Finance Act Cap 23:04 Sec 22P); Sec 39 amended VAT Act Cap 23:12 Sec 12B to impose 10% VAT on exported unbeneficiated ore & concentrate (0% on lithium sulphate) payable in USD; Sec 31 mandated Quoted Price Method transfer pricing
Stated_Government_Objective: Increase fiscal capture, penalize low-value concentrate exports via VAT Act Sec 12B, incentivize sulphate refining, and curb transfer pricing.
Target_Material_or_Product: Unbeneficiated lithium ore, lithium concentrate, lithium sulphate
Implementation_Evidence: Producers (incl. Bikita) petitioned for tax relief in Oct 2026 citing working capital pressure and price volatility.
Researcher_Interpretation: Confirmed via legal analysis of Finance Act (No. 7) of 2025: the 10% charge is legally classified as VAT under Sec 12B of the VAT Act [Cap 23:12], distinct from the 3% export levy under Cap 23:04.

Policy_Title: Immediate Suspension of Raw Mineral and Lithium Concentrate Exports (Stage 1: Suspension)
Instrument_Number: Ministry of Mines Press Statement (25 Feb 2026)
Policy_Mechanism: Immediate indefinite suspension of all raw mineral and lithium concentrate exports, explicitly including shipments already in transit
Stated_Government_Objective: Halt illicit stockpiling (e.g. at Port of Beira), curb export malpractices/under-invoicing, and accelerate sulphate plant construction.
Target_Material_or_Product: All raw minerals and lithium concentrates (incl. in-transit shipments)
Enforcement_Agency: Ministry of Mines and Mining Development; ZIMRA; MMCZ
Implementation_Evidence: Primary Ministry press statement confirmed immediate border halt on 25 Feb 2026; superseded for compliant producers by April 2026 quota regime (POL_08).
Researcher_Interpretation: Stage 1 of 2026 export shock: abrupt enforcement accelerated the Jan 2027 deadline by 10 months.

Policy_Title: Transitional Concentrate Export Quotas (Stage 2: Conditional Resumption)
Policy_Mechanism: Allowed partial resumption of concentrate exports under company-specific quotas conditioned on written commitments to build lithium sulphate plants before Jan 1, 2027
Stated_Government_Objective: Prevent export revenue collapse while enforcing binding beneficiation commitments ahead of Jan 2027.
Enforcement_Agency: Ministry of Mines and Mining Development; MMCZ
Implementation_Evidence: Sinomine (Bikita) received 200,000 t + 300,000 t quotas; Information Minister Nick Mangwana confirmed on Oct 9, 2026 no extension beyond Jan 2027.
Researcher_Interpretation: Stage 2 of 2026 export shock: pragmatic accommodation for large Chinese incumbents without abandoning the Jan 2027 cutoff.

Policy_Title: Parliamentary Record on 2027 Export Prohibition, Beneficiation Plans, & Monthly Returns
Policy_Mechanism: Records January 2027 concentrate-export prohibition, mandatory beneficiation plans, and monthly production & employment returns
Stated_Government_Objective: Institutionalize beneficiation compliance and regularize state monitoring of mine-level output and jobs.
Target_Material_or_Product: Lithium concentrates; mine-level production and employment data
Enforcement_Agency: Parliament of Zimbabwe; Ministry of Mines and Mining Development
Implementation_Evidence: Documented in Nov 11, 2026 parliamentary proceedings ahead of Jan 2027 cutoff.
Researcher_Interpretation: Adds legislative oversight and mandatory monthly production/employment reporting to executive SIs.
